title: SQS messaging — concept map
intro: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a managed message queue that buffers work between producers and consumers. Standard queues offer high throughput and best-effort ordering; FIFO queues guarantee order and deduplication within a message group. Consumers pull messages, process them, then delete — but only after the visibility timeout window. When processing fails repeatedly, Dead Letter Queues (DLQs) isolate poison messages. Lambda, SNS, and EventBridge are common producers; idempotent handlers are mandatory because delivery is at-least-once.

overviewDiagram.title: SQS producer-consumer flow
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart LR
  P[Producer\nAPI / SNS / EventBridge] -->|SendMessage| Q[(SQS Queue)]
  Q -->|ReceiveMessage| C[Consumer\nLambda / ECS / EC2]
  C -->|DeleteMessage on success| Q
  C -->|fail / timeout| Q
  Q -->|maxReceiveCount exceeded| DLQ[(Dead Letter Queue)]

conceptCards.title: Standard vs FIFO
conceptCards.summary: Standard: unlimited throughput, best-effort order. FIFO: .fifo suffix, message groups, deduplication ID.
conceptCards.example: Order pipeline uses FIFO with orderId as MessageGroupId

conceptCards.title: Visibility & DLQ
conceptCards.summary: Hidden message reappears after visibility timeout. Redrive policy sends poison pills to DLQ after N receives.

conceptCards.title: Lambda consumer
conceptCards.summary: Event source mapping polls SQS, invokes Lambda in batches. ReportBatchItemFailures for partial retry.

conceptCards.title: SNS / EventBridge fan-out
conceptCards.summary: One event fans to many SQS queues. Filter policies route by attribute. SQS buffers downstream spikes.

conceptCards.title: Idempotency
conceptCards.summary: At-least-once delivery means duplicates. Use idempotency keys in DynamoDB or conditional writes.
conceptCards.example: paymentId stored before charge; skip if already processed
